items.stem: When does choosing a smaller, cheaper model make sense?

options.text: When the task is simple enough that the smaller model does it correctly
options.rationale: Correct: match the model to the task; a smaller model suffices for simple work.

options.text: Never; always use the largest model
options.rationale: Always using the largest model wastes cost on simple tasks.

options.text: Only when cost is literally zero
options.rationale: Cost is rarely zero; the decision is about task fit.

options.text: Whenever you are in a hurry, regardless of correctness

items.explanation: Correct: match the model to the task; a smaller model suffices for simple work.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO steps reduce Cursor cost without guessing? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Measure where spend concentrates before optimising
options.rationale: Correct: measuring targets the real cost drivers.

options.text: Trim context to what the task actually needs
options.rationale: Correct: smaller context cuts cost and latency.

options.text: Skip tests to save model calls
options.rationale: Cutting tests trades away correctness, not waste.

options.text: Dump the whole repo into every prompt
options.rationale: Oversized context raises cost with no benefit.

items.explanation: Correct: measuring targets the real cost drivers.

items.stem: A proposed cost saving would skip the review step on AI-written changes. What is the right call?

options.text: Reject it; correctness and review must not be traded for cost
options.rationale: Correct: skipping review to save cost ships unreviewed risk.

options.text: Accept it to hit the budget
options.rationale: Hitting a budget by removing review is a false saving.
The day does not change the risk.

options.text: Accept it and remove tests too

items.explanation: Correct: skipping review to save cost ships unreviewed risk.
